source_text: Secundum haec, inquit, faciebant prophetis patres eorum. o Christum uersipellem, nunc destructorem nunc adsertorem prophetarum! destruebat ut aemulus, conuertens discipulos eorum sibi, adserebat ut amicus, suggillans insectatores eorum.
pass_a_gloss: According to these things, he says, the fathers of the prophets were doing. Oh Christ, shape-shifter, now destroyer now defender of the prophets! He was destroying as a rival, turning their disciples to himself, he was defending as a friend, rebuking their persecutors.
pass_b_english: He says their fathers treated the prophets this way. Oh Christ, you shape-shifter — now the prophets' destroyer, now their defender! He destroyed them as a rival, turning their disciples to himself; he defended them as a friend, rebuking their persecutors.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent in meaning and agency. The term 'uersipellem' is correctly rendered as 'shape-shifter'.
